newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner sees more expansion in fund management.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner sees more expansion in fund management.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG said on Thursday its expansion drive in global fund management was not yet at an end.

Following its acquisition last year of San-Francisco-based RCM Capital Management, Dresdner chairman Juergen Sarrazin told a news conference the bank was still on the look-out for more potential takeover targets, especially in the U.K. and Europe.
"Our expansion in this field is not at all at an end," Sarrazin said. "There can certainly be changes from the present situation."
Sarrazin said that Dresdner was not holding concrete talks with a particular fund manager but was merely keeping its eyes open.

RCM Capital Management, consolidated into group accounts as of June 1996, is to control Dresdner's newly created Dresdner RCM Global Investors group, which will manage the bank's institutional asset management business outside Germany.
Dresdner said it now had 330 billion marks in assets under management, counting private and institutional business.
